rubric.evidence: IDL for both WebTransportOptions members and both WebTransport attributes copied verbatim from the W3C Editor's Draft dated 18 November 2026 (sections 6.3 and 6.9). Spec history traced via git: PR #574 merged 2024-02-27 as 8db4c499. Chrome behaviour read from Chromium source on 2026-11-22: dedicated_web_transport_http3_client.cc sets initial max streams to max(100, hint) only when the hint is non-null; web_transport.cc setters only update the stored slot (comment: used during session establishment, not sent post-handshake). Error behaviour from the WPT file anticipated-concurrent-incoming-streams.https.any.js (TypeError for -1, 65536, +/-Infinity, NaN; rejected assignment leaves the value unchanged).
rubric.notes: MDN's property pages say the browser 'can take the new value into account in its later negotiations'; the page discloses that Chrome 158 does not, citing source.

rubric.evidence: Feature id 5089961022980096 appears in the live milestone=158 listing under 'Enabled by default' with listing name 'WebTransport anticipated concurrent incoming streams' (fetched 2026-11-22); slug derived from that listing name. Runtime feature WebTransportAnticipatedConcurrentIncomingStreams is status stable at trunk; Chrome 158 is the current stable per BCD browsers/chrome.json (released 2026-11-17). The detail record's stale 'Proposed' status text is disclosed.

Case A stub: MDN has dedicated property pages for both attributes (Value, Exceptions, Description, examples, Specifications, Browser compatibility; modified 2026-11-12) and the constructor page documents both options plus the TypeError. Stub exemption applies; no reference-contract.json. The quick reference adds what MDN does not track: Chrome timing of the hint, the 100 floor in Chromium, intent/LGTMs, runtime flag, BCD gaps.
Examples delegated to MDN's two worked examples per property; the embedded showcase allowance-tuner demo constructs a real WebTransport with hints and reads them back.

BCD api/WebTransport.json values quoted (Chrome 158, Firefox 161, Safari 26.4, mirrors). Firefox 161 is labelled beta (BCD browsers/firefox.json, release 2026-11-24). BCD has no constructor-option subfeature for these members, stated explicitly. Baseline: web-features does not yet map these BCD keys, so the banner reports parent webtransport Baseline newly (2026-03-24, webstatus.dev) separately from the gendn-computed limited availability of the members.
rubric.notes: When Firefox 161 ships, the banner should flip to newly available once web-features maps the keys.

deno task responsive auto-scan ok on both classes; screenshots read at 360px DPR3 and 1280px plus full-length 360x4200 and 1280x2600 captures: no horizontal overflow, banner list wraps, long member names wrap via overflow-wrap:anywhere, table contained.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive reference documentation page with data tables that do not overflow on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Wrap tables in an overflow container with tabindex=0, role=region and an accessible name so keyboard users can scroll it; keep header semantics.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: .table-wrap gets tabindex=0, role=region, aria-labelledby=quick-reference and a :focus-visible outline; rows use th scope=row. Exception: no stacked layout, because this is a two-column key/value table that already wraps at 360px.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Mobile and desktop screenshots from deno task responsive --screenshots, read 2026-11-22

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive reference documentation page with data tables that do not overflow on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsic sizing and let long unbreakable content wrap rather than force page overflow.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: overflow-wrap:anywhere on h1, lede and inline code; iframe max-width:100%; baseline browser list uses flex-wrap.

openQuestions: Does a future Chrome renegotiate when the attribute is set on a connected transport (the spec setter is a SHOULD)? Chrome 158 source says no.
web-features has not yet mapped the api.WebTransport.anticipatedConcurrentIncoming* BCD keys; their own Baseline status is unpublished.

followUpGoals.goal: After Firefox 161 ships (2026-11-24) and web-features maps the anticipatedConcurrentIncoming* keys, update the Baseline banner from limited to the published status for these members.
